title.zh: 摸脉搏的那一小块地方
title.en: The Small Patch Where You Take a Pulse

text.zh: 手腕内侧那一小块能摸到跳动，是因为这里恰好有一条动脉浮到了骨头和皮肤之间。它是怎么走到这儿的？
text.en: You can feel a beat on the inner wrist because an artery happens to surface there, caught between bone and skin. How did it get to that spot?

text.zh: 起点在锁骨底下，紧贴着第一根肋骨。它常年压在骨面上，把肋骨压出了一道浅槽。
text.en: It starts under the collarbone, pressed hard against the first rib. Year after year of that pressure has worn a shallow groove into the bone.

text.zh: 穿过腋窝之后它换了名字，顺着上臂内侧往下走。量血压时袖带勒住的正是这一段——把它压扁再慢慢放开，就能听出压力。
text.en: Past the armpit it changes name and runs down the inner side of the upper arm. This is the stretch a blood-pressure cuff squeezes: flatten it, release it slowly, and the pressure announces itself in sound.

text.zh: 到肘窝一分为二，一条走拇指那侧，一条走小指那侧，两条并行下到手掌，再在掌心连成一个环。
text.en: At the crook of the elbow it splits in two, one running down the thumb side and one down the little-finger side, both reaching the palm and joining there into a loop.

text.zh: 前臂里有两根骨头并排走。拇指侧这根到手腕这一头变得又宽又扁，正好给血管垫出一个平台。
text.en: Two bones run side by side through the forearm. The one on the thumb side broadens and flattens towards the wrist, which happens to give a vessel somewhere firm to lie on.

text.zh: 小指侧那根在手腕这一端反而细下去，让开了位置。翻手掌时，是拇指侧那根绕着它转，它自己基本不动。
text.en: The one on the little-finger side does the opposite, tapering away at the wrist and leaving room. When you turn your palm over, the thumb-side bone pivots around this one, which barely moves at all.

text.zh: 拇指侧那条最后浮上来的地方，恰好在这条粗肌肉的腱和骨头之间。是这块肌肉的边缘把它顶到了皮下。
text.en: The thumb-side vessel surfaces exactly between the tendon of this thick muscle and the bone. It is the edge of this muscle that pushes the artery up under the skin.

text.zh: 它内侧还并着一条腱。你摸脉时手指按下去先碰到的那道硬棱，多半就是它，而不是血管。
text.en: A tendon runs alongside it on the inner side. When you press for a pulse, the firm ridge your fingertip meets first is usually this, not the vessel.

text.zh: 再往中间还有一条更细的，位置就在腕横纹正中。有意思的是，这一条不是人人都有。
text.en: Further towards the middle lies a thinner one, sitting right at the centre of the wrist crease. The curious thing is that not everyone has it.

text.zh: 回程还有一套走在皮下。外侧这条从手背一路爬到肩前，隔着皮肤就看得见——手背上鼓起的"青筋"就是它的起点。
text.en: The trip back also has a set running just under the skin. This one climbs the outer side from the back of the hand to the front of the shoulder, visible through the skin — those raised cords on your hand are where it begins.

text.zh: 手上用过的血从另一套管道回来，在锁骨下方汇进胸腔。全身的淋巴液也在这个夹角处并进血流——两套循环在这里合成一套。
text.en: Blood that has done its work in the hand returns by a separate set of pipes and enters the chest below the collarbone. All the body’s lymph also joins the bloodstream at that same angle — two circulations becoming one.

text.zh: 内侧那条走得深一些。两条之间在肘窝有一段斜的桥接——静脉穿刺挑的常常就是这座桥。
text.en: The one on the inner side runs deeper. A slanting bridge joins the two at the crook of the elbow, and that bridge is often exactly what a needle is aiming for.

text.zh: 能摸到脉搏并不是巧合。那一小块地方，是骨头、肌腱和一条恰好没被埋深的动脉挤在一起的结果。
text.en: Finding a pulse there is no accident. That small patch is what happens when bone, tendon and one artery that never got buried deep all crowd into the same place.
